items.title: Forgejo v18.0.0
items.description:
## Release notes - Breaking security features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14148): Move internal communication to UNIX socket. The `INTERNAL_TOKEN` can now be dropped from the configuration, and the UNIX socket path can be configured using the `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` options. This change removes the `./forgejo generate secret INTERNAL_TOKEN` command and updates the contrib Forgejo systemd unit file. The `forgejo.service` example systemd file has been updated to set `RuntimeDirectory=forgejo`, which is a recommended setting for all systemd users.
See the [documentation](https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/config-cheat-sheet/#server-server) for more information. - User Interface features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14038): adds inline copy buttons for new repo instructions - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14299): add reload protection to file dropzone and code review comments - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14425): allow users to preview fonts in the ui - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14536): make dropdowns dialog-based with various improvements - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14158): accessible aria-labels & working commit description toggles w/o JS - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14522): disable text wrapping in code blocks - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/13517): auth: start oauth2 login if its the only available login - User Interface bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14435): Fix icons in milestone and project metadata not being consistent with how icons are used elsewhere on Forgejo - Features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14386): feat(lfs): add lfs file support to /render endpoint - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14571): enh: add org members to other teams without invitation - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14117): team membership provenance tracking - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/13023): add code suggestion - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14505): feat(feed): parse and set limit parameter for release feed request - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14164): feat(cmd): allow password to be read from stdin - User Interface changes without a feature or bug label - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14598): sort user repositories in package linking, make input searchable - Other changes without a feature or bug label - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14703): use DB index when accessing API `GET /{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=...` - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14621): deleting a user w/ repo-specific access tokens or authorized integrations causes foreign-key violation - Included for completeness but not user-facing (chores, etc.) - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14508): refactor: migrate relative-time component to Typescript - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14633): fix(CLI): settings not loaded for create-authorized-integration - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14713): chore: keep locale instructions out of readme, only link to relevant resources - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14666): refactor: migrate svg component to Typescript - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14689): Actions logs are not transferred to object storage when last UpdateLog has no rows - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/10065): uses lang attribute to set the right language for tippy tooltip - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14564): refactor: migrate JS configs to Typescript - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14664): refactor: migrate utils component to Typescript - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14538): refactor: migrate emoji component to Typescript - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14692): chore: fix forgejo branch - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14628): prevent in-db branch state rollback from concurrent pushes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14269): Use the minus (−) sign instead of hyphen (-) for better alignment with the plus (+) sign - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14685): chore: fix release notes for PR 14148 - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14688): Update dependency katex to v0.18.10 (forgejo) - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14687): Update dependency @lezer/highlight to v1.2.5 (forgejo) - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14642): unblock concurrency group job if previous run finished by server-side evaluation - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14680): output error message when internal socket can't be created - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14665): Update dependency @codemirror/lang-liquid to v6.3.3 (forgejo) - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14652): enh: enable maintainer edits by default on new repositories - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14667): fix(tests): fix flaky TestConvertInvitedUserWithExpiry - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/12757): fix descriptions generated from struct comments - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14606): Update dependency htmx.org to v2.0.11 (forgejo) - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14629): accept Arch Linux packages with non-zero epoch - items.title: refactor: migrate DOM utils to Typescript
items.body:
This PR converts our `dom.js` utils to Typescript, adding appropriate types along the way. This continues !14508's scoped approach to tightening our frontend type-checks, in line with the feedback in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/5859#issuecomment-2560264.

This one was a doozy to get right, but I checked through all the call sites for these that I could grep for, and I think I managed to write type annotations that accurately describe these functions' invariants and their current usage throughout the codebase. I also fixed some incorrect documentation about certain parameters. As a result, our tooling can enforce those invariants more soundly, making it easier to audit around new uses of these functions and to trim down existing uses later on (e.g. jQuery removal over time).

As a bonus, jQuery has type declarations now (via `@types/jquery`), which will make further TS ports and refactors easier to reason about in the meantime.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> We must not update `@types/jquery` past the semver-major version of `jquery` we have installed. I'm not sure how best to represent that to Renovate when the package versions don't match, but I can look into that if someone else doesn't get to it first, lol.

issue.title: problem: deleting a user fails with "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" when the user has a repo-scoped access token
issue.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

Small self-hosted homelab instance with one admin and a few service accounts for automation. One of the service
accounts was created for a single job and given a token scoped to one repository. When that job was retired I tried
to delete the account.

### Problem description

Deleting a user fails with `500 DeleteUser: deleteBeans: foreign key constraint violation: FOREIGN KEY constraint
failed`. It happens through the admin UI, through `DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{username}`, and also with
`?purge=true`. The user owns no repositories and no organizations.

I reproduced it on a `.backup` copy of the SQLite database. The user had an access token created with a
per-repository scope (`write:repository` on one repo). That scope is stored in `access_token_resource_repo`, which
has a foreign key `token_id` -> `access_token.id`. Deleting the user deletes the user's `access_token` rows without
first deleting the matching `access_token_resource_repo` rows, so SQLite rejects it. With foreign keys enabled on
the copy, `DELETE FROM user WHERE id=N` alone succeeds, while `DELETE FROM access_token WHERE uid=N` fails until
the `access_token_resource_repo` row is removed.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a user and add it as a collaborator on a repository.
2. As that user, create an access token scoped to that single repository (for example `write:repository`).
3. As an admin, delete the user (UI or API).

Expected: the user and its tokens, including their per-repository scope rows, are deleted.

### Potential workarounds

Back up the database, delete the user's row from `access_token_resource_repo`, then delete the user normally
(the API returned 204 afterwards and the user was gone).

A user that is still a member of an organization must first be removed from it; that is a separate, clear error
(`user still has membership of organizations`) and is not part of this bug.

### Forgejo Version

16.0.3 (`16.0.3+gitea-1.22.0` as reported by `/api/v1/version`), database schema version 305.

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), running in an unprivileged LXC container
- Deployment: the `forgejo` binary from the release download, run by a systemd unit (`forgejo web --config /etc/forgejo/app.ini`); no Docker
- Database: SQLite (sqlite3 CLI 3.46.1 used for the reproduction)
- Reverse proxy in front: nginx (Nginx Proxy Manager)
- No LDAP or other external authentication sources

### Solutions

items.title: enh(api): resolve, unresolve and reply to pull request review conversations
items.body:
### Existing problems this enhancement addresses

A pull request review can be answered over the API, but its conversations can never be closed
over it. In Forgejo 16.0.5:

- There is no endpoint to resolve or unresolve a review conversation. The web UI does it through
  POST /{owner}/{repo}/issues/resolve_conversation, which needs a browser session and a CSRF token,
  so an API token cannot reach it.
- There is no endpoint to reply in an existing conversation. The closest is
  POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/reviews/{id}/comments, which creates a comment by path
  and line. On a stale review (the branch was rebased or pushed since), the line no longer matches,
  and the comment lands as a new one on the current code instead of as a reply in the thread.

So tools that work on pull requests through the API (CI bots, review bots, MCP servers used by
coding agents) can address every point of a review and still leave every thread open. Someone has
to open the browser and click "Resolve conversation" on each one. It also makes it impossible to
tell, from the API alone, which addressed points the author considers done.

### Enhancement description

Add API endpoints for the two actions the web UI already offers on a review conversation:

- POST   /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/comments/{id}/replies
  Reply in the conversation the comment belongs to, with the same threading the UI uses, whether
  or not the review is stale. Body: {"body": "..."}.
- POST   /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/comments/{id}/resolve
- DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/comments/{id}/resolve
  Mark the conversation resolved or unresolved, with the same permission check as the web action
  (the PR author, or anyone with write access).

Reads need no change: PullReviewComment already carries `resolver`.

### Details and notes

- Version checked: Forgejo 16.0.5+gitea-1.22.0, against the instance's /swagger.v1.json. The
  review endpoints present are list/create/get/submit/delete review, list/create/get/delete review
  comment, and dismiss/undismiss; nothing for resolving or replying.
- The web route for resolving exists (resolve_conversation, with action=Resolve|UnResolve and
  comment_id), so this is exposing an existing action, not adding new behaviour.
- The paths above are a suggestion; nesting under /reviews/{id}/comments/{comment} would work as
  well, if that fits the existing API better.
- Use case that hit this: an agent addressed every point of a review over the API, posted a summary
  comment, and could not close a single thread.

items.title: bug: Actions run builds the previous commit after a failed refs/pull/N/head update, but reports status on the new head
items.body:
### Can you reproduce the bug on the Forgejo test instance?

No, I can't try it on the test instance for some reason

### Description

When two or more pushes to PR branches of the same repository land at nearly the same moment, the
`refs/pull/N/head` update for one of them can fail, while the synchronize event for it still fires. The
Actions run for that PR then checks out the old commit, but its commit status is written to the new head.
A PR can show a green check for a commit that was never built.

My best interpretation:
1. Each push runs its own `TestPullRequest`. `PushToBaseRepo` does `git fetch file://<repo> refs/heads/<branch>`
   and then sets `refs/pull/N/head` (`services/pull/pull.go`).
2. Forgejo runs git with `fetch.writeCommitGraph=true` (`modules/git/git.go`), so every such fetch rewrites the
   commit-graph and takes `commit-graph-chain.lock`. Git does not wait for that lock; a concurrent fetch into the
   same repository exits 128.
3. On that error the ref is not updated and the loop continues, but the `isSync` path still calls
   `PullRequestSynchronized` for the PR (the `err == nil` check there tests a different error).
4. The Actions notifier resolves the run commit from `refs/pull/N/head` (`services/actions/notifier_helper.go`),
   which is still the old commit, while the payload's `pull_request.head.sha` comes from the branch
   (`services/convert/pull.go`) and the commit status is written to that new head
   (`services/actions/commit_status.go`).

To reproduce:
- Open several PRs on one repository and push to their branches at the same moment (for example, merging the
  base branch into each of them in a loop).
- Some runs show `GITHUB_SHA` different from `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, and `refs/pull/N/head` lags the
  branch until the next push.
- Outside Forgejo, eight concurrent `git fetch file://... refs/heads/bN` into one repository with
  `fetch.writeCommitGraph=true` gave 2 lock failures in a single trial; with it set to `false`, none.

My take:
Either the ref update is retried or serialised (the code already notes that `TestPullRequest` should become a
queue), or a PR whose ref update failed does not emit a synchronize event, so no run reports on a commit it did not
build.

Workaround:
A workflow step that fails when `GITHUB_SHA` differs from `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`; pushing a new commit
to the branch repairs the ref.

### Forgejo Version

15.0.3

### How are you running Forgejo?

Self-hosted, Docker image, Kubuntu native. The relevant code looks unchanged on main.

### Logs

services/pull/pull.go:324:TestPullRequest() [E] PushToBaseRepo: exit status 128 - fatal: Unable to create
'/data/git/repositories/<owner>/<repo>.git/./objects/info/commit-graphs/commit-graph-chain.lock': File exists.

### Database

SQLite

### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

Small self-hosted homelab instance with one admin and a few service accounts for automation. One of the service
accounts was created for a single job and given a token scoped to one repository. When that job was retired I tried
to delete the account.

### Problem description

Deleting a user fails with `500 DeleteUser: deleteBeans: foreign key constraint violation: FOREIGN KEY constraint
failed`. It happens through the admin UI, through `DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{username}`, and also with
`?purge=true`. The user owns no repositories and no organizations.

I reproduced it on a `.backup` copy of the SQLite database. The user had an access token created with a
per-repository scope (`write:repository` on one repo). That scope is stored in `access_token_resource_repo`, which
has a foreign key `token_id` -> `access_token.id`. Deleting the user deletes the user's `access_token` rows without
first deleting the matching `access_token_resource_repo` rows, so SQLite rejects it. With foreign keys enabled on
the copy, `DELETE FROM user WHERE id=N` alone succeeds, while `DELETE FROM access_token WHERE uid=N` fails until
the `access_token_resource_repo` row is removed.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a user and add it as a collaborator on a repository.
2. As that user, create an access token scoped to that single repository (for example `write:repository`).
3. As an admin, delete the user (UI or API).

Expected: the user and its tokens, including their per-repository scope rows, are deleted.

### Potential workarounds

Back up the database, delete the user's row from `access_token_resource_repo`, then delete the user normally
(the API returned 204 afterwards and the user was gone).

A user that is still a member of an organization must first be removed from it; that is a separate, clear error
(`user still has membership of organizations`) and is not part of this bug.

### Forgejo Version

16.0.3 (`16.0.3+gitea-1.22.0` as reported by `/api/v1/version`), database schema version 305.

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), running in an unprivileged LXC container
- Deployment: the `forgejo` binary from the release download, run by a systemd unit (`forgejo web --config /etc/forgejo/app.ini`); no Docker
- Database: SQLite (sqlite3 CLI 3.46.1 used for the reproduction)
- Reverse proxy in front: nginx (Nginx Proxy Manager)
- No LDAP or other external authentication sources

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

feat: add headings to common repository webpages (#14204)

To begin addressing #7653 and #10363, this PR adds top-level headings to most public Repository pages, including:
- Issues (Open, Closed, All)
- Labels
- Milestones (Open, Closed)
- Pull requests (Open, Closed, All)
- Projects (Open, Closed)
- Releases
- Tags
- Packages
- Wiki (list with pages present)
- Activity (Pulse, Contributors, Code frequency, Recent commits)
- Actions (All workflows, Named workflow, No workflows)

The change adds some new translation strings, and new template logic on the relevant pages to display translatable text as headings. The re-used existing translation strings seem to have already been used elsewhere in similar contexts, and therefore seemed intuitive for inclusion as page headings as well.

The attached video `headings-first-go.webm` shows me slowly clicking through the new pages, with their headings, in the order listed above, navigating from the page "Open issues", to "Closed issues", to "All issues", to "Labels", to "Open milestones", etc. This video does not include Packages, Wiki, Activity, or Actions.

The additional attached videos show the Pulse page (the default repo Activity view), whose heading now reads "Activity between September 2, 2026 and September 9, 2026", then proceeding to the various other activity pages. Each page's load state has been lengthened to demonstrate the new heading layouts, including error states.

This PR only adds headings to Repository pages for now. Several other Forgejo webpages are also affected by #7653, and some pages might also do well with additional explanatory text, documentation links, etc. (What the heck is a "Milestone" anyway, to someone who hasn't seen the concept at another forge?) I can add such explainers in this PR if that is wanted, or we can save these for discussion later. I welcome feedback on this point.

## Testing these changes

1. Open Forgejo locally using `make build frontend && test-e2e-debugserver`
2. Navigate to the above-named pages
3. Look at headings, ensure consistency.

You may test most headings at any repository, many have all units enabled. For Actions, consider testing at `/user2/test_action_run_search/actions`. You may need to log in to `user2` first. (The password is `password`).

To test Activity failure states, consider adding `await sleep(4000)` to the start of the `fetchGraphData` method, just after `isLoading` is first set, in `web_src/js/components/Repo*.vue` as appropriate, then exit the devserver during the load state.

items.title: Fix commit status reporting for scheduled workflows
items.body:
While going through the logs of my self-hosted Forgejo instance, I found over 100K `head commit is missing in event payload` errors in 30 days. This was a result of scheduled Actions jobs whose stored event was push but the payload only had the schedule action.

So when creating schedules and runs we should record the event explicitly and also for existing runs, use the stored commit SHA for the status.

I'm not very familiar with how to add the appropriate unit tests.

items.title: refactor: migrate DOM utils to Typescript
items.body:
This PR converts our `dom.js` utils to Typescript, adding appropriate types along the way. This continues !14508's scoped approach to tightening our frontend type-checks, in line with the feedback in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/5859#issuecomment-2560264.

This one was a doozy to get right, but I checked through all the call sites for these that I could grep for, and I think I managed to write type annotations that accurately describe these functions' invariants and their current usage throughout the codebase. I also fixed some incorrect documentation about certain parameters. As a result, our tooling can enforce those invariants more soundly, making it easier to audit around new uses of these functions and to trim down existing uses later on (e.g. jQuery removal over time).

As a bonus, jQuery has type declarations now (via `@types/jquery`), which will make further TS ports and refactors easier to reason about in the meantime.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> We must not update `@types/jquery` past the semver-major version of `jquery` we have installed. I'm not sure how best to represent that to Renovate when the package versions don't match, but I can look into that if someone else doesn't get to it first, lol.
